meta.title: CenterPoint and Houston's power, 17 days of posts
meta.subject: CenterPoint Energy and electric service in the Houston region — outages and storm response, rate cases and bills at the PUC, the resiliency plan and vegetation management, legislative accountability measures aimed at the utility, and CenterPoint's transmission and generation build
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 17, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about CenterPoint Energy and Houston's power, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Rates, bills and utility profits
lanes.description: CenterPoint is overcharging customers through rate hikes, riders and inflated line items like streetlights, putting shareholder profit ahead of ratepayers.

lanes.label: PUC and Legislature accountability
lanes.description: The PUC, lawmakers and investigators need to scrutinize CenterPoint's costs, demand invoices and transparency, and impose penalties or reforms.

lanes.label: Transmission, generation and data centers
lanes.description: CenterPoint's transmission and generation build and large-load additions like data centers are either needed growth or a cost shifted onto ordinary customers.

lanes.label: Outages and storm response failures
lanes.description: CenterPoint leaves Houston-area customers without power after storms like Beryl, with slow restoration and poor communication, and is to blame.

lanes.label: Resiliency plan and tree trimming
lanes.description: Whether the resiliency plan, pole and line hardening and vegetation management actually make the grid more reliable, or are a costly promise.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.name: KPRC 2 Houston
posts.text: CenterPoint streetlight costs jump more than 10,000% in one Houston-area community. ENOUGH asks why. https://t.co/ddThdt24JG

posts.name: KPRC 2 Houston
posts.text:
A Katy-area MUD paid $24,009 for seven streetlights in 2025. Five years earlier, 36 lights in the same community cost $1,190. 

CenterPoint cites higher material, labor and underground boring costs but declined to provide underlying invoices to ENOUGH. Customers can contact the PUCT if they believe charges exceed the approved tariff.
